build_avatar_url.description: Turn any text into the address of a unique picture: a robot, a monster, a cat or a human avatar, always the same one for the same text. Nothing is downloaded, so this is the cheap way to give a record a profile picture, fill an empty avatar slot or put a face beside a name in an email. No API key required.
build_avatar_url.display_str_template: Build a Robohash avatar URL for {0}.
build_avatar_url.name: build_avatar_url

parameters.description: The text to turn into a picture: a user id, an email address, a filename, an IP address, anything at all. The same text always gives the same picture, and a different one gives a different picture, so pass whatever identifies the thing the avatar stands for.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Optional. Which artwork to build the picture from. Leave it empty for the classic robots, which is what Robohash does by default. Pick one set to pin every picture to that style; pick several and the text decides which of them each picture comes from, which keeps a long list from looking uniform. 'Any set' hands the same decision to Robohash across all of its sets, so a set added later can change pictures that already exist. Human avatars is the one to reach for when the picture stands in for a person.
parameters.name: image_sets

parameters.description: Optional. Put a background behind the picture, chosen from the text like everything else. No background by default, which leaves a PNG transparent so it sits on any colour. Choose one where a transparent picture would disappear, such as a dark chat theme.
parameters.name: background

parameters.description: Optional. Pin every robot to one colour, for a set of avatars that matches a brand. Only the Robots set is drawn in every colour, so this cannot be combined with another set. Left alone, the text picks the colour, which is what makes an untouched list look varied.
parameters.name: color

parameters.description: Optional. How wide the picture should be, in pixels. 300 by default; anything from 1 to 4096.
parameters.name: width

parameters.description: Optional. How tall the picture should be, in pixels. 300 by default; anything from 1 to 4096. The artwork is square, so a different width and height stretches it.
parameters.name: height

parameters.description: Optional. The file format. PNG by default, which is the one that keeps a transparent background. JPEG is smaller but is flattened, so a picture with no background lands on black. The format travels as a file extension on the text, which Robohash removes again before hashing, so the same text gives the same picture in every format.
parameters.name: image_format

parameters.description: Optional, and rarely wanted. Off by default, so the same text gives the same picture whichever format you ask for. Turn it on and the extension counts as part of the text, so the PNG and the JPEG of one text are two different pictures. This is Robohash's 'ignoreext=false'.
parameters.name: hash_extension

parameters.description: Optional. Off by default. Turn it on and the link shows the person's own Gravatar picture when they have one, falling back to a generated picture when they do not, so a directory shows real faces without leaving gaps. Choose the second option when the text is an email address and the third when it is already an MD5 hash of one. Get an avatar for an email address does the same thing and downloads the file.
parameters.name: gravatar

description: Turn any text into a unique picture. Give Robohash a user id, an email address, a filename or an IP address and it hands back a robot, a monster, a cat, a human avatar or a cosmic ape that is always the same for that text and different for every other, which is what makes it the stand-in for a profile picture nobody has uploaded yet. Build a link to embed, build a whole list of them for a team in one step, or download the picture as a file to attach or upload. Six styles, two backgrounds, ten robot colours and any size up to 4096 pixels, and for email addresses it can show the person's own Gravatar when they have one and a generated picture when they do not. No account or API key required.
